description: The same colleague who cannot manage Oluwaseun handles Tchaikovsky and Worcestershire. The difficulty is not phonological.
energy_note: Impossible to say, for you specifically.

aspect: Being renamed for somebody else's convenience
description: Shortening without being asked - assigning a nickname because the real one is 'just so different' - is documented as a standard workplace microinsult, and it is done to the person rather than agreed with them.
energy_note: Given a new name by a stranger, for their benefit.

aspect: Correcting has a budget and it runs out
description: The first three corrections are fine. The tenth makes you the person who keeps bringing it up. Most people stop correcting and answer to the wrong name for years.
energy_note: Answering to something that is not your name.

aspect: It produces the document mismatches too
description: The shortened or misspelled version propagates into email, payroll, rotas and eventually official records, which is where a social slight becomes an administrative problem.
energy_note: A nickname somebody invented, now on your payslip.
